BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.

From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook. The Seller's documents have been treated as counterparty material, not instructions.

## Preliminary Points

1. **"FINAL / agreed at principal level / market standard" claims are rejected.** The preamble says these positions were settled by both deal teams and are not to be re-opened. Under playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3, nothing is agreed unless it is confirmed through our own authority process. We have no record of Amelia Frost approving any of these positions. The "market standard" ranges in the preamble are the Seller's assertion, and our playbook sets our positions.
2. **The facts are stale.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Today is 4 November 2026. Before Completion we should require an updated disclosure or bring-down covering Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006 and the bonuses. We should not assume anything has changed, in either direction, without evidence.
3. **The Disclosure Letter partly undercuts the Seller Update.** The letter itself confirms several gaps:
   - no Bluefen consent;
   - no Riverlark repayment or discharge;
   - no Ironquay payment receipt;
   - bonuses missing from the funds flow;
   - DD-006 unresolved.

   We should use these admissions in the mark-up.

## Issue-by-Issue Review

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at AUD 6,000,000. The 20% figure matches our conditional fallback, but that fallback needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft, and none has been given. A number matching a fallback does not clear it.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000. Only the excess above the basket is recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000. Seller liable from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (tipping).
- **Recommendation:** Reject and restate our numbers and the tipping mechanism. The Seller's thresholds are 5x ours, and the deductible structure would permanently remove AUD 250,000 of recoverable loss.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months for general claims (cl 12.3). The Seller also proposes that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general claims. Separate, longer periods for Fundamental/Title claims and fraud.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at 24 months. 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. The "applies to all Claims" default must also be struck, because it is a hidden override of the special regimes.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties sit under the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime with a 100% cap (AUD 24,000,000) and at least six years. It must sit outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright. Title and capacity go to whether we receive what we are paying for, so capping them at 20% for 18 months is unacceptable.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No carve-out. The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5) apply to "all Claims of any nature", which would capture fraud.
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert an express carve-out. This is non-waivable under our playbook, and no deal-team member has authority to concede it.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room as at 22 September 2026 (DL 1.1), plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records (DL 1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only, against identified warranties, with enough detail for us to assess the matter.
- **Recommendation:** Delete DL 1.1 and 1.2. Whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure is expressly rejected by our playbook. Specific disclosures (DL 2 to 10) can stand only to the extent they are fair and specific.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer "or its advisers" knew, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the blanket exclusion. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must:
  - apply to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry;
  - never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3. It is a constructive-knowledge bar that, combined with whole-data-room disclosure, would gut the warranties, including over matters the Seller itself has flagged.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition treated as satisfied on delivery of Bluefen's written consent. DL 2 admits there is no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - effective consent, plus evidence that its cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a condition precedent to Completion;
  - no "consent-on-delivery" deeming;
  - an obligation stronger than reasonable endeavours.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue, so a conditional or ineffective consent is a material deal risk.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release "to be provided following Completion" for roughly AUD 3,200,000 outstanding. DL 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is available.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - a current payout letter;
  - direct repayment from Completion funds;
  - effective security releases (including PPSR) delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. That route is permitted only with an irrevocable lender undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, and neither exists. An unreleased change-control facility is also inconsistent with a debt-free price.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. DL 5 does not address payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item or treated as Debt, or funded by the Seller. A specific indemnity should back this up.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the silent exclusion. The bonuses are a Company liability triggered by Completion, so "a matter for the Seller" with no mechanism leaves the cost with us.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The cl 11.1 indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment and described as "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** A broader indemnity covering any Ironquay claim to the Project Materials, IP ownership or licence, and any related loss. It should preserve the SOW3 cure (payment of every SOW3 fee triggers transfer under DD-004 cl 7.3) and require a confirmatory assignment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow form. DL 4 confirms there is no payment receipt and no assignment. The AUD 180,000 open in DD-010 is unverified either way, so the indemnity should not be pegged to that figure.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - log preservation;
  - a proper investigation, including into whether access occurred, the scope of the export, and any notification assessment;
  - regular updates before Completion;
  - appropriate warranty and indemnity protection.

  We should not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss figure.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept the "not material" characterisation, and do not overstate the issue either. About 1,240 records went to an unintended recipient, and whether anyone accessed them is unknown. Until the investigation is complete, the risk cannot be sized.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals totalling AUD 330,000, described as "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of DD-008 and DD-011 read together, covering:
  - timing and scope;
  - whether each renewal is avoidable or terminable;
  - accrual and ordinary-course status;
  - any related-party aspect.

  The renewals should not be automatically classified as Debt, nor automatically accepted as ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** Hold the position pending diligence and request the underlying facts. DL 8 itself declines to say whether the renewals are ordinary course, so the Seller's label is not established.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Title, capacity, Tax and IP are folded into the general regime. Default language ("applies to all Claims unless expressly stated", "all Claims of any nature") overrides the special categories.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate, express regimes for Title, Tax, IP, payment or indemnity claims, and covenants. None of them should be subject to a hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and strike the catch-all language in cl 12.3 / 13 / 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5. These are drafting overrides that would quietly cap everything at the general levels.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register. DL 10 concedes that this identifies only the Seller's source and is not verification by the Buyer.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence covering:
  - title and ownership (ASIC records, issue history, share certificates);
  - absence of encumbrances (a PPSR search, and releases covering the Riverlark security);
  - Seller authority and capacity (board approvals and constitution).
- **Recommendation:** Reject reliance on DD-012 alone. An internal register supplied by the Seller does not prove title independently.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP positions are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP treated as OPEN, with their own regimes to be negotiated. We should not assume these are settled, and we should not assume unlimited liability either.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "settled" characterisation. There is no authority-confirmed agreement, so these terms remain open for negotiation.

## Escalation and Next Steps

- **No concessions without authority.** Nothing in this draft justifies using any fallback (the 20% cap, the 18-month period, or a post-Completion Riverlark release) without Amelia Frost's written authority identifying this draft. If the team wants to consider any fallback, it should be escalated to her with this review.
- **Request a refresh of facts, dated after 22 September 2026,** covering:
  - Bluefen consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied;
  - a Riverlark payout letter and draft releases;
  - Ironquay payment evidence and a confirmatory assignment;
  - the bonus on-cost calculation;
  - the DD-006 investigation status;
  - the Sandbar contracts.
- **The mark-up should respond in substance.** Our response to Seller counsel should be a full mark-up. It should state plainly that we do not accept that any position is final or agreed.
